text: I'll start with the pod and the cluster capacity.

arguments.root_cause_statement: Deployment fraud/fraud-scoring asks each replica for 512 whole CPU cores. The unit suffix is missing: "512" means 512 cores, not the 512m (half a core) that was intended. The only node in the cluster, incident-lab-control-plane, has 6 allocatable CPU, so the scheduler can never place the pod and rejects it with "0/1 nodes are available: 1 Insufficient cpu". The pod fraud-scoring-596445859d-thcdh therefore stays Pending with PodScheduled=False and node <none>, the Deployment reports ready=0/1, and no fraud scores are produced. Fixing it requires editing the Deployment's pod template (the pod itself is disposable and would be recreated with the same request).
arguments.mechanism: Deployment fraud/fraud-scoring sets .spec.template.spec.containers[scorer].resources.requests.cpu to "512" (512 whole cores) instead of "512m"; the only node has cpu=6/6 allocatable, so the default scheduler rejects the pod with "0/1 nodes are available: 1 Insufficient cpu. preemption: 0/1 nodes are available: 1 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling." and the replica stays Pending with PodScheduled False and no node assigned, keeping the Deployment at ready=0/1.

evidence.claim: The paged Deployment has no ready replicas and its only pod is Pending and unscheduled.
The pod is Pending with no node assigned and PodScheduled False.
The scheduler rejects the pod for insufficient CPU on the only node.
evidence.quote: 0/1 nodes are available: 1 Insufficient cpu. preemption: 0/1 nodes are available: 1 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling.

evidence.claim: The pod requests 512 CPU (whole cores, no milli suffix).
The Deployment pod template is the source of the unsuffixed CPU request.
The cluster's single node has only 6 allocatable CPU, far below the 512 cores requested.

ruled_out.alternative: The node is tainted, NotReady, or otherwise unavailable, blocking scheduling
ruled_out.ruling_claim: The single node reports Ready=True and no taints are recorded; the scheduler's own reason is Insufficient cpu, not a taint mismatch.

ruled_out.alternative: A nodeSelector or affinity rule in the pod spec prevents placement
ruled_out.ruling_claim: The pod has no node selector at all, so no placement constraint other than resources applies.

ruled_out.alternative: A ResourceQuota or LimitRange in the fraud namespace is rejecting or inflating the pod
ruled_out.ruling_claim: The namespace contains only a ConfigMap and a ServiceAccount besides the workload; no ResourceQuota or LimitRange exists, and the pod was admitted and created successfully.
ruled_out.quote: fraud Normal SuccessfulCreate replicaset/fraud-scoring-596445859d x1 Created pod: fraud-scoring-596445859d-thcdh

ruled_out.alternative: The container image or command is broken (crash/image pull failure)
ruled_out.ruling_claim: The pod never reached a node, so no image pull or container start was ever attempted; the only condition present is PodScheduled False.
